translation: adj. 按时的，准时的，守时的
definitionEn: arriving, happening, or doing something at the agreed or expected time

posExamples.sentence: She is always punctual for morning meetings.
The train made a punctual departure at nine.
Punctual payment helps a business maintain trust.

wordForms.other: punctuality = punctual + -ity; unpunctual adds the negative prefix un-

collocations.translation: 准时参加某事；介词用 for
collocations.example: Please be punctual for the interview.
The service is known for punctual departures.
The landlord expects punctual payment of the rent.

collocations.translation: 准时到达；副词修饰 arrive
collocations.example: Every speaker arrived punctually.
She is perfectly punctual in her work.
Commuters value a punctual bus service.
He keeps punctual hours even at weekends.
The course requires punctual attendance.

synonyms.example: The lecture began on time.
synonyms.usage: 介词短语，常作表语或状语：be on time / arrive on time；punctual 是形容词，可作表语或前置定语，常形容人、到达或服务。

synonyms.example: Thank you for your prompt reply.
synonyms.usage: 形容词，可作前置定语或表语，强调行动迅速及时，常搭配 prompt reply/action/payment；punctual 更强调符合约定时间。

advancedExpressions.expression: punctual → unpunctual；punctual + -ity → punctuality
advancedExpressions.example: Repeated unpunctuality may damage professional trust.

advancedExpressions.expression: be punctual for sth / arrive punctually / arrive on time
advancedExpressions.example: She was punctual for class and arrived punctually every day.

advancedExpressions.expression: Participants are expected to be punctual for ...
advancedExpressions.example: Participants are expected to be punctual for the opening ceremony.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She is always punctual for morning meetings.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: She is always punctual for morning meetings, arriving five minutes early with every document ready.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留同一人物和晨会守时场景，用现在分词补充具体可见的守时行为

sentenceUpgrade.original: The train made a punctual departure at nine.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The train made a punctual departure at nine, despite the heavy snow that had delayed road traffic.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留列车九点准点出发的事实，用 despite 增加阻碍条件，突出 punctual

classPractice.question: All candidates are expected to be punctual ____ the interview.
classPractice.note: be punctual for sth 表示“准时参加某事”。

classPractice.note: 修饰动词 left 用副词 punctually。

classPractice.question: Please arrive on time for the meeting. → Please be ____ for the meeting.
classPractice.note: be punctual for = arrive on time for。

translation: n. 概述，纵览，概论，概况
original_sentence: The 7 Habits—An Overview We are what we repeatedly do.
definitionEn: a short general description that gives the main facts or features of a subject

posExamples.sentence: The chapter provides an overview of the seven habits.
Read the course overview before choosing your modules.
The diagram gives a clear overview of the process.

wordForms.other: compound noun: over + view; plural: overviews

collocations.translation: 《七个习惯——概述》（课文标题词块）
collocations.example: The section is headed “The 7 Habits—An Overview”.
The article offers an overview of habit formation.
The first paragraph provides an overview of the topic.
Let me begin with a brief overview.
The chart gives a general overview of the results.
The book provides a comprehensive overview of the field.
The project overview lists the main goals.
Mind maps help learners gain an overview of complex ideas.

synonyms.example: Write a short summary of the passage.
synonyms.usage: 可数名词，常作 give/write/read a summary of；侧重压缩原文要点。overview 常作 an overview of，侧重展示整体结构和范围。

synonyms.example: The course is a survey of modern history.
synonyms.usage: 名词，常用于学术课程或系统综述，作 a survey of；overview 更简短、更一般，可用于报告、项目和图表。

advancedExpressions.expression: An Overview signals that the section will present the main framework rather than every detail.
advancedExpressions.example: The heading gives readers an overview before the detailed discussion.

advancedExpressions.expression: begin with a brief overview of ...
advancedExpressions.example: The presentation begins with a brief overview of the problem.

advancedExpressions.expression: gain an overview of = get a broad picture of
advancedExpressions.example: The timeline helps us get a broad picture of the event.

sentenceUpgrade.original: This part tells us the main ideas of the seven habits.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: This section provides a concise overview of the seven habits.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 provide an overview of 替换宽泛的 tell us the main ideas。

sentenceUpgrade.original: First, I will briefly describe the project.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I will begin with a brief overview of the project.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 begin with a brief overview 构成正式演示开场。

classPractice.question: The opening chapter gives an overview ____ the whole course.
classPractice.note: an overview of sth 为固定搭配。

classPractice.note: brief overview 表示“简要概述”。

classPractice.question: The diagram gives a clear ____ (overview / detail) of the whole process.
classPractice.note: whole process 提示需要表示整体概览的 overview。

translation: n. 合成物，混合物，复合材料 adj. 合成的，混成的，复合的
definitionEn: made from several different parts or materials; a thing formed in this way

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 合成图像；由多幅图像合成的画面
uncommonMeanings.example: The final photograph is a composite of several images.
Twelve is a composite number because it has more than two factors.

posExamples.sentence: The frame is made from a lightweight composite material.
The portrait is a composite of three photographs.
A composite score combines several separate results.

wordForms.other: component (n. 组成部分); composite comes from Latin componere, 'put together'

collocations.example: The cable is protected by a composite material.
The cover uses a composite image.
The final ranking is based on a composite score.
Researchers created a composite index of well-being.
Nine is a composite number.
The police released a composite portrait.

collocations.phrase: a composite of A and B
collocations.example: The design is a composite of tradition and innovation.
The software creates a composite from several layers.

synonyms.example: Water is a chemical compound.
synonyms.usage: 形容词常作前置定语 compound word/interest；名词多指化合物或复合物。composite 强调不同部分组合成整体，常搭配 material/image/score。

synonyms.example: The teams achieved a combined score of 90.
synonyms.usage: 过去分词形容词，通常置于名词前 combined effort/result，强调合并后的总量；composite 更强调内部由多个成分构成。

advancedExpressions.expression: compose (组成) → composition (构成) → composite (复合的/合成物)
advancedExpressions.example: The composite is composed of several layers.

advancedExpressions.expression: a composite measure / index of ...
advancedExpressions.example: The study uses a composite measure of academic progress.

advancedExpressions.expression: composite = whole made of parts; component = one part of a whole
advancedExpressions.example: Each component contributes to the composite score.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The material has several different parts.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The device is made from a lightweight composite material.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 composite material 凝练“由多种部分构成的材料”。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The score combines many results.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The researchers reported a composite score based on several indicators.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 composite score 和 based on 明确综合指标来源。

classPractice.question: Carbon fibre is often used as a lightweight ____ material. (composite / separate)
classPractice.note: composite material 表示“复合材料”。

classPractice.question: The final image is a composite ____ five separate photographs.
classPractice.note: a composite of ... 表示“由……组成的合成物”。

classPractice.question: A wheel is one ____ (component / composite) of a bicycle.
classPractice.note: component 指整体中的一个组成部分；composite 指由多部分组成的整体。

translation: vt. 取得（成果），收获
definitionEn: to cut and collect a crop; to obtain something, especially as a result of one's actions

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 获得，收获（尤指努力或行为带来的结果）
uncommonMeanings.example: Students who practise consistently reap lasting benefits.

posExamples.sentence: Farmers reap the wheat in late summer.
The team reaped the rewards of careful preparation.
Good habits allow us to reap long-term benefits.

wordForms.other: reap–reaped–reaped; sow (播种) is its common contrast

idioms.translation: 种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆；自食其果
idioms.example: If we ignore small bad habits, we may eventually reap what we sow.

collocations.example: Farmers reap a rich harvest in autumn.
Regular readers reap the benefits of a wider vocabulary.
She finally reaped the rewards of years of practice.
The company reaped large profits from the invention.
Careless planners eventually reap the consequences.
The students reaped the fruits of months of practice.
Healthy routines help us reap long-term gains.

collocations.phrase: sow the seeds and reap the harvest
collocations.translation: 播种并收获；先付出后收获
collocations.example: Education sows the seeds from which society reaps the harvest.

synonyms.example: Farmers harvest rice in the autumn.
synonyms.usage: 及物或不及物动词，也可作名词，主要接 crops/rice/data；reap 作动词既接庄稼，也常接抽象宾语 benefits/rewards/profits。

synonyms.example: She gained valuable experience abroad.
synonyms.usage: 及物动词，宾语常为 experience/knowledge/advantage；语义中性。reap 通常暗示结果来自此前投入或行为。

advancedExpressions.expression: as you sow, so shall you reap
advancedExpressions.example: As you sow, so shall you reap: daily choices gradually shape character.

advancedExpressions.expression: reap the rewards of = benefit from = gain from
advancedExpressions.example: Students reap the rewards of disciplined practice.

advancedExpressions.expression: reap benefits that extend far beyond ...
advancedExpressions.example: Good time management brings benefits that extend far beyond the classroom.

advancedExpressions.expression: sow a seed of kindness and reap the fruit of a warm heart
advancedExpressions.example: Sow a seed of kindness, and you may reap the fruit of a warm heart.（课件仿写：sow... and reap...）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Good habits give us benefits.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: By maintaining good habits, we can reap substantial long-term benefits.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 reap benefits 替换 give us benefits，并加 by doing 表方式。

sentenceUpgrade.original: She worked hard and was rewarded.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: She eventually reaped the rewards of years of persistent effort.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 reap the rewards of 和 persistent effort 强化因果。

classPractice.question: Those who exercise regularly will ____ the benefits in later life.
classPractice.note: reap the benefits 表示“获得益处”。

classPractice.question: After years of effort, the team finally reaped the ____ (reward).
classPractice.note: reap the rewards 常用复数，表示“获得回报”。

classPractice.question: 良好的学习习惯会带来长期收益。
classPractice.answer: Good study habits will bring / reap long-term benefits.
classPractice.note: 可用 reap long-term benefits 表示“获得长期收益”。

translation: n. 命运，天命，天数
definitionEn: the things that will happen to someone in the future, especially those believed to be beyond their control

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 命中注定要成就的事业或角色
uncommonMeanings.example: She believed it was her destiny to teach.

posExamples.sentence: Small daily choices can shape our destiny.
He believed that becoming a doctor was his destiny.
The community took its destiny into its own hands.

wordForms.other: be destined for sth / be destined to do sth

idioms.idiom: be the master of one's own destiny
idioms.example: Proactive people try to be the masters of their own destiny.

collocations.example: Repeated actions shape our destiny.
She felt ready to fulfil her destiny.
Education can help people control their destiny.
No one can predict the project's ultimate destiny.
The leader spoke with a strong sense of destiny.
The two ideas were destined to conflict.
The invention seemed destined for success.
Some people believe in destiny, while others stress personal choice.

synonyms.example: They accepted their fate calmly.
synonyms.usage: 名词，常见搭配 suffer/meet/decide one's fate，语气常较消极或强调不可避免；destiny 常可含积极使命或未来方向。

synonyms.example: His fortunes changed after the discovery.
synonyms.usage: 名词，可指 luck 或 wealth，常见 good fortune / make a fortune；指命运时常用复数 fortunes。destiny 不表示财富。

advancedExpressions.expression: destiny → destine → destined; be destined to do / for sth
advancedExpressions.example: A habit repeated daily may be destined to become part of character.

advancedExpressions.expression: take control of one's own destiny
advancedExpressions.example: Self-discipline enables young people to take control of their own destiny.

advancedExpressions.expression: shape one's destiny = determine one's future course
advancedExpressions.example: Our choices determine the future course of our lives.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Our habits decide our future.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The habits we cultivate today gradually shape our destiny.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用定语从句 we cultivate today 和 shape our destiny 提升表达。

sentenceUpgrade.original: She decided her own future.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: She refused to leave her future to chance and took control of her own destiny.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 refuse to leave...to chance 与 take control of 构成对比。

classPractice.question: Daily choices gradually ____ our destiny.
classPractice.note: shape one's destiny 表示“塑造某人的命运”。

classPractice.question: The young scientist seemed destined ____ success.
classPractice.note: be destined for sth 表示“注定会有……”。

classPractice.question: She decided to control her own future. → She decided to take control of her own ____.
classPractice.note: take control of one's own destiny 表示“掌控自己的命运”。

translation: n. 格言，箴言，座右铭
definitionEn: a short statement expressing a general truth or rule of conduct

posExamples.sentence: The teacher began with a familiar maxim about habits.
“Actions speak louder than words” is a useful maxim.
He tried to live by the maxim that honesty is the best policy.

wordForms.other: plural: maxims; do not confuse maxim with maximum

collocations.example: The speech opens with a well-known maxim.
The old maxim still holds true today.
Children learn moral maxims through stories.
The judge referred to a legal maxim.
She follows the maxim that practice makes progress.
He lives by the maxim “Never stop learning”.
Effective leaders follow the maxim of putting people first.
The educator coined a maxim that students remembered.

synonyms.example: “A stitch in time saves nine” is a proverb.
synonyms.usage: 可数名词，常指民间长期流传、形式固定的生活智慧；maxim 也可由个人提出，更侧重行为准则。

synonyms.example: As the saying goes, practice makes perfect.
synonyms.usage: 可数名词，最宽泛，常用固定结构 as the saying goes；maxim 较正式，通常表达一般真理或行为原则。

advancedExpressions.expression: maxim (行为准则) / proverb (民间谚语) / motto (个人或组织座右铭)

advancedExpressions.expression: As the old maxim goes, ...

advancedExpressions.expression: turn a maxim into a daily practice

sentenceUpgrade.original: People often say that actions matter more than words.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As the familiar maxim goes, actions speak louder than words.

sentenceUpgrade.original: He believed honesty was important.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: He lived by the maxim that honesty is the best policy.

classPractice.question: He lives ____ the maxim that honesty is the best policy.

translation: n. （系船用的）缆绳，（支撑桥梁等用的）钢索；电缆
original_sentence: As Horace Mann, the great educator, once said, “Habits are like a cable.

uncommonMeanings.example: The family received a cable announcing his safe arrival.

posExamples.sentence: The habit grew stronger like a cable woven strand by strand.

collocations.translation: 习惯如同缆绳（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: As Horace Mann once said, “Habits are like a cable.”

collocations.phrase: a cable made of twisted strands
collocations.translation: 由绞合线股制成的缆绳
collocations.example: The bridge is supported by cables made of twisted strands.

The signal travels through a fibre-optic cable.

The programme first appeared on cable television.

Disconnect the cable before repairing the device.

synonyms.example: The lamp is connected by a thin wire.

synonyms.example: Keep the electrical cord away from water.

advancedExpressions.expression: Habits are like a cable: each repeated action adds another strand.

advancedExpressions.expression: power cable / cable car / cable television / fibre-optic cable
advancedExpressions.example: The cable car runs beside a line of power cables.

advancedExpressions.expression: wire is a thin conductor; cord is a flexible lead; cable is a thick bundle
advancedExpressions.example: Several wires are bound together inside the cable.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Habits become strong through repetition.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Like a cable woven strand by strand, a habit gains strength through daily repetition.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The workers put a line under the road.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The workers laid a fibre-optic cable beneath the road.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 lay a cable 和 fibre-optic 精确说明工程动作与对象。

classPractice.question: Workers are preparing to ____ a power cable beneath the street.

classPractice.question: 习惯如同一根缆绳。Habits are ____ ____ ____ .

posExamples.sentence: We weave a strand of the cable every day.

collocations.phrase: weave a strand of it every day

sentenceUpgrade.original: We repeat an action every day and the habit becomes strong.

classPractice.question: A loose strand ____ hair had fallen across her face.

translation: n. （天然或人造、擦洗物品用的）海绵块；（用以填充家具、垫子等的）人造海绵
original_sentence: The well-known Chinese writer Lu Xun said, “Time is like the water in a sponge.
definitionEn: a soft light material full of small holes that can absorb liquid; also a simple sea animal with a porous body

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 靠别人养活的人（非正式，含贬义）
uncommonMeanings.example: He became a sponge who expected his friends to pay.
Sea sponges live attached to the ocean floor.

posExamples.sentence: Time is like the water in a sponge.
Wipe the surface with a damp sponge.
Children can absorb language like a sponge.

wordForms.other: compound uses: bath sponge, kitchen sponge, sea sponge

idioms.example: Despite several setbacks, the team refused to throw in the sponge.

idioms.translation: 揩某人的油，靠某人养活
idioms.example: He should work rather than sponge off his family.

collocations.translation: 海绵里的水（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Lu Xun compared time to the water in a sponge.
Clean the board with a damp sponge.
Replace the kitchen sponge regularly.
A sea sponge filters water for food.

collocations.phrase: absorb / soak up water like a sponge
collocations.example: Dry soil can soak up water like a sponge.
Wipe the table with a clean sponge.
Squeeze the sponge to remove the water.

collocations.translation: 像海绵一样善于吸收信息
collocations.example: Young learners are often like sponges.

synonyms.example: The seat is filled with soft foam.
synonyms.usage: 不可数名词，指人造泡沫材料或液体泡沫；sponge 可指天然／人造吸水块，也指海绵动物。

synonyms.example: Use a scouring pad for the dirty pan.
synonyms.usage: 可数名词，专用于擦洗顽固污渍，表面较粗糙；sponge 更柔软、吸水，适合普通清洁。

advancedExpressions.expression: Time is like the water in a sponge: if you squeeze, you can always get some.
advancedExpressions.example: The metaphor suggests that spare time can be found through effort.

advancedExpressions.expression: absorb information like a sponge
advancedExpressions.example: Curious learners absorb new ideas like a sponge.

advancedExpressions.expression: sponge off sb = live at another person's expense
advancedExpressions.example: He refused to sponge off his parents.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Young children learn new words very quickly.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Young children absorb new language like a sponge.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 like a sponge 比喻快速吸收信息。

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As Lu Xun's sponge metaphor suggests, spare time appears when we are willing to squeeze.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 引用课文 sponge/squeeze 比喻并用 as 引出依据。

translation: vi. & vt. 挤压，捏；（使）挤入，挤过，塞入
original_sentence: If you are willing to squeeze, you will always get some.” Time is a finite resource, but with a little effort you can always find the time to do what needs to be done.
definitionEn: to press something firmly, especially from opposite sides; to force something into or through a small space

uncommonMeanings.example: I can squeeze an hour into the afternoon.
Small shops were squeezed out of the market.

posExamples.sentence: The editor squeezed another chart onto the final page.
Passengers squeezed past one another at the doorway.
She squeezed his shoulder in silent encouragement.

wordForms.other: squeeze–squeezed–squeezed; common particles: in, out, through, into

idioms.example: The lift held all of us, but it was a tight squeeze.

collocations.translation: 愿意去挤（时间）（课文原句比喻）
collocations.example: If you are willing to squeeze, you will always get some time.

collocations.phrase: squeeze water from / out of a sponge
collocations.example: She squeezed water from the sponge.
Squeeze the juice from half a lemon.
We squeezed through the narrow gap.
Six people squeezed into the car.
She squeezed his hand reassuringly.
I can squeeze in a short meeting.
High costs squeezed small firms out.

synonyms.example: Press the button firmly.
synonyms.usage: 及物或不及物动词，强调施加压力，常接 button/hand/surface；squeeze 通常从两侧用力挤压，常为取出液体或挤进空间。

synonyms.example: The machine compresses the waste.
synonyms.usage: 及物动词，较正式，强调减小体积或数据大小，常接 gas/file/material；squeeze 更日常，也可表示挤过、挤进。

advancedExpressions.expression: squeeze time from a finite schedule as water is squeezed from a sponge
advancedExpressions.example: Small intervals can be squeezed from an apparently full day.

advancedExpressions.expression: squeeze in / squeeze out / squeeze through / squeeze into
advancedExpressions.example: She squeezed in a meeting before squeezing through the crowded station.

advancedExpressions.expression: squeeze a sponge / squeeze sb's hand / squeeze through a gap
advancedExpressions.example: He squeezed her hand before they squeezed through the doorway.

advancedExpressions.expression: squeeze in time for sb / squeeze every spare minute into sth
advancedExpressions.example: She squeezed in a ten-minute call with her parents, which strengthened their emotional bond.（课件仿写）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I found time for a short meeting.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I managed to squeeze in a short meeting before lunch.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 squeeze in 表示在紧凑日程中勉强安排。

sentenceUpgrade.original: They moved through the narrow opening.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: They turned sideways and squeezed through the narrow opening.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 squeeze through 与动作细节 turned sideways 增强画面。

classPractice.note: squeeze through 表示“挤过”。

classPractice.note: squeeze in 表示“勉强安排进时间表”。

classPractice.question: 她从海绵中挤出了水。She ____ the water ____ of the sponge.
classPractice.note: squeeze sth out of sth。

translation: adj. 有限的，有限制的
original_sentence: If you are willing to squeeze, you will always get some.” Time is a finite resource, but with a little effort you can always find the time to do what needs to be done.
definitionEn: having a definite limit or end; not infinite

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 数学中的有限的（元素数量或数值范围有界）
uncommonMeanings.example: The set contains a finite number of elements.

posExamples.sentence: The committee had only finite funds for the entire project.
A finite sequence ends after a fixed number of terms.
The planet's usable land is finite.

wordForms.other: finite ↔ infinite; Latin finis means 'end'

collocations.translation: 有限资源（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Time is a finite resource.
We have a finite amount of time.
The task must be completed in finite time.

collocations.phrase: a finite supply of clean water
collocations.example: The region has a finite supply of clean water.
Human attention has a finite capacity.
The options form a finite set.
Every device has a finite lifespan.
Planning reflects the finite nature of time.

synonyms.example: We have limited time.
synonyms.usage: 形容词，常作前置定语或表语，日常用法广，可指数量少或受限制；finite 更正式，强调存在明确终点或界限，与 infinite 对立。

synonyms.example: The values lie within a bounded range.
synonyms.usage: 形容词，常用于数学、科学或正式语境，强调边界；finite 强调数量或持续时间不是无限，但不一定强调空间边界。

advancedExpressions.expression: Time is a finite resource, so priorities involve choice.
advancedExpressions.example: Because time is finite, every commitment carries an opportunity cost.

advancedExpressions.expression: finite ↔ infinite; finiteness / infinity
advancedExpressions.example: A finite schedule cannot contain an infinite number of tasks.

advancedExpressions.expression: human attention is a finite cognitive resource
advancedExpressions.example: Multitasking divides a finite cognitive resource.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The committee had only finite funds for the entire project.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The committee had only finite funds for the entire project, so every proposal had to justify its long-term value.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留项目资金有限的场景，用 so 结果分句说明资源约束下的决策标准

sentenceUpgrade.original: A finite sequence ends after a fixed number of terms.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A finite sequence ends after a fixed number of terms, unlike an infinite sequence that continues without limit.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留有限数列的数学事实，用 unlike 对比澄清 finite 与 infinite

translation: vt. & vi. 进行头脑风暴，集思广益提出（想法或办法）
original_sentence: For example, you can use mind maps to brainstorm ideas, take notes, plan your writing and learn new words.
definitionEn: to produce many ideas quickly, usually in a group and without judging them at first

posExamples.sentence: Students brainstormed names for the new science club.
The designers held a silent brainstorming exercise.
Before judging any proposal, brainstorm as many alternatives as possible.

wordForms.other: brain + storm; brainstorm ideas/solutions, brainstorm with sb

collocations.phrase: use mind maps to brainstorm ideas
collocations.translation: 用思维导图集思广益（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: You can use mind maps to brainstorm ideas.
The class brainstormed solutions to the problem.
We held a short brainstorming session.
She brainstormed with her teammates.
Let's brainstorm about possible topics.

collocations.translation: 集思广益想办法做某事
collocations.example: They brainstormed ways to save time.
Always brainstorm before writing the first draft.
Brainstorm freely before evaluating each idea.

synonyms.example: The exercise generated several useful ideas.
synonyms.usage: 动词短语，主语可为人、活动或工具，强调结果；brainstorm 通常指个人或小组在暂不评价的情况下快速提出许多想法。

synonyms.example: The design team ideated several new products.
synonyms.usage: 及物或不及物动词，多见于设计和商业语境，较专业；brainstorm 更普遍，课堂与团队会议中常用。

advancedExpressions.expression: use mind maps to brainstorm, organize and connect ideas
advancedExpressions.example: A mind map records ideas before they are classified.

advancedExpressions.type: 课堂流程·先发散后评价
advancedExpressions.expression: brainstorm freely first; evaluate and classify later
advancedExpressions.example: Separate idea generation from judgement.

advancedExpressions.expression: brainstorm ideas / brainstorm with sb / brainstorm about sth
advancedExpressions.example: We brainstormed with the class about possible solutions.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Think of some ideas before writing.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Use a mind map to brainstorm and organize ideas before drafting.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 brainstorm 与 organize 构成写作前两步流程。

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The team held a focused brainstorming session and generated several workable solutions.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 brainstorming session 和 generate solutions 提升团队协作语体。
